title: The path and payload of the separation-of-duty check, the incident channel, the text of MSG-P4-006 and the approval route of a new conflict version are not specified for the app slice
description: (a) The check the sign-in calls has no path, request or answer in any source: Architecture v5 slide 14 names POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) and gives rwb-access no separation-of-duty operation, the Ownership Map has no api row for it, and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists neither, so the base of Template and Rules §R4 is applied by rule and the payload is stated by this revision. (b) AC1 requires an incident to the security administrator and FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 names the security administrator queue, while no source names an incident queue, an incident operation or a target service and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives the service no event and no incident path. (c) MSG-P4-006 is named by three FSD P4 v3 exception rows and carries no text in any source, while the legacy message table holds MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003 only. (d) AC2 requires a new separation of duty version that is approved, and the legacy Endpoints table gives the two rule-version paths, which the Ownership Map ruling gives to P7 rwb-decision and to the rule-version stories of this service; no source names the operation that approves a version of role_conflict, and the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON is the only named route. (e) The parameter that carries the environment code recorded on a refusal entry is named by no source, and the refusal entry's own fields are the library's.
source: RWB-AD-005 sections Story, Acceptance criteria, Data, Endpoints, Permission checks, Validation and messages and Test cases; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03, AC-EXC-P4-002-03 and AC-EXC-P4-003-05; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211), T3.2, T6.1 and appendix T-A (API-P4-007, API-P4-012); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 41 and 44; Ownership Map v1 (role_conflict owned by P4; no api row for a separation-of-duty path)

area: Separation of duty, refusal record, message text and conflict-version approval
legacy_ref: RWB-AD-005 AC1, AC2, Endpoints, Validation and messages
owner_role: rwb-access service owner with the security administrator role owner and the audit owner
proposed: Publish the check as POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise/separation-of-duty on the base of §R4 and DP-13 with a payload stated by this revision; carry the incident as the recorded refusal addressed to RW-SECADM until an incident operation exists; keep the ID MSG-P4-006 and leave its text to the business, reconciling it with RWB-P4-E1022-APP; load a version through the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and let the check resolve the version in force; read the environment code through the parameters contract

title: The check path and payloads, the name of the conflict-version field of the session answer and the rights of the two administrative reads are this contract's decision and not a source value
description: (a) The separation-of-duty check has no path, request or answer in the Ownership Map or in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A, and Architecture v5 slide 14 names only POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), so the base, the path suffix and the four schema shapes are stated by this revision and confirmed by no source. (b) API-P4-012 GET /me/session states in its purpose that it answers roles, scope, matrix and conflict versions, and declares no field name and no field list, so the name conflictVersion and its shape are this revision's choice. (c) The two administrative reads of role_conflict have no api row; they sit on the /admin family of this service and take the Platform administration R letter of TSD P4 v3 T6.1, which is applied by analogy and not by a row. (d) The refusal of a session carries no event in any source: the FSD requires a refusal event with reason ROLE_CONFLICT, Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access no such event and slide 43 gives it AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged only, so the refusal is declared as the decision record and the load and approval route of a new version is named as the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON rather than declared here.
source: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211), T3.2, T6.1 and appendix T-A (API-P4-007, API-P4-012); FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 41, 43 and 44; Ownership Map v1 (role_conflict owned by P4; GET /admin/roles and GET /me/session are the P4 path rows); RWB-P4-E1037-CON (the session read and the load path)

owner_role: contract owner of rwb-access with the sign-in contract owner and the session contract owner
proposed: Publish POST /authorise/separation-of-duty, GET /admin/role-conflicts and GET /admin/role-conflict-versions/{versionId} on /api/recovery/access/v1; name the one field conflictVersion in the session answer of RWB-P4-E1037-CON without restating that operation; take Platform administration R for both reads; declare the refusal as the decision record and name the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON as the route of a new version
